title: Absolute moment of a Gaussian linear functional
statement: Let $n\ge 0$, let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$, and let $L:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be linear and continuous. Then $\int |L(z)|\,d\gamma_n(z)=2\varphi(0)\sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^n L(e_i)^2}$, where $e_i$ are the coordinate unit vectors and $\varphi$ is the standard Gaussian density; the equality is understood as an equality of nonnegative extended integrals, with the finite right-hand side embedded in $[0,\infty]$.
hypotheses_covered: $L$ is a continuous linear functional on $\mathbb R^n$
replaced: Let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$ and $X,Y$ independent with that law. For a linear functional $L:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$, put $|L|_2=\sqrt{\sum_i L(e_i)^2}$, where $e_i$ is the canonical basis. The nonnegative extended expectation satisfies $\mathbb E|L(X)|=|L|_2\,2\varphi(0)$, with the finite expression on the right embedded into $[0,\infty]$ and $\varphi$ the standard Gaussian density.
